## A1-1965 — RestartSource completion means graceful stop, failure unexpected termination

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> component: silver-commons/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/commons/kafka/TopicSubscriber.scala; operation: Feat/TT-5945 allow setting number of consumers per pod for topic subscriber; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Concern stated in the source:** Never means subscriber started or failed-to-start

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> `RestartSource.onFailuresWithBackoff` sets `maxRestarts = Int.MaxValue`, i.e. this future shouldn’t complete with a failure
> 
> ```
> * Wrap the given [[Source]] with a [[Source]] that will restart it when it fails using an exponential backoff.
> *
> * This [[Source]] will never emit a failure, since the failure of the wrapped [[Source]] is always handled by
> * restarting. The wrapped [[Source]] can be cancelled by cancelling this [[Source]].
> * When that happens, the wrapped [[Source]], if currently running will be cancelled, and it will not be restarted.
> * This can be triggered simply by the downstream cancelling, or externally by introducing a [[KillSwitch]] right
> * after this [[Source]] in the graph.
> *
> * This uses the same exponential backoff algorithm as [[akka.pattern.Backoff]].
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> But ok if we don’t trust akka, then these 2 log entries are a bit misleading
> 
> * On Success, it means that the kafka subscription has been gracefully stopped. This is either during graceful shutdown, or something really went wrong \(cuz we don’t really stop our kafka consumer for normal topic - only the TaskTopicSubscriber supports this\). Nevertheless, it surely doesn’t mean “the subscriber has started”
> * On Failure, then something unexpected went wrong with the `RestartSource`. But it also doesn’t mean “the subscriber failed to start”, it just means the subscription stream was terminated with \(potentially fatal\) error
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.
- Unlimited restarts; cancellation/kill switch controls stop; TaskTopicSubscriber special case.

**Evidence:** anon-1.jsonl:1986 · comment 626763164 · PR 11658 · 2025-04-30

Source path: `silver-commons/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/commons/kafka/TopicSubscriber.scala`

**Explicit source context (pr_title):**

> Feat/TT-5945 allow setting number of consumers per pod for topic subscriber

**Context:**

**Concern stated in the source:** Empty default instructions cannot distinguish never-initialized from upserted-then-deleted plan state.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> The entity state is default with empty fee instructions, it means the plan always exists, just without any data. Modelling it this way means you can’t distinguish between a uninitialized plan vs a plan with upserted-then-deleted fee instructions.
> 
> If we care enough about this, then we probably should make state a sealed trait, default with case object NotInitialized, otherwise it’s case class Initialized\(feeInstructions\). Then you can throw for GetCmd/DeleteCmd on NotInitialized. And no-op without error if deleting already deleted fee instruction for Initialized, and even throw if deleting last entry for Initialized \(to ensure there’s always an entry to support the fee rate query\)

**Conditions and limits:**

- The sealed NotInitialized/Initialized state is conditional on caring about that distinction; no-op deletion and last-entry rejection are proposals within that model.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A2-0469 — BffServiceImpl: In on-behalf operations:

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 10258 ([INV-3639] feat(bff): Capture and propagate Customer/Employee context in BFF), bff-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/bff/impl/BffServiceImpl.scala; original row 469.

**Concern stated in the source:** In on-behalf operations:

* auth user would be employee, which we would set into context using EmployeeProvider
* and the request \(either payload or query param\) should specify the customer, which we would use to validate proper ownership/relationship in guards

‌

Once it reaches the handler \(logic layer\), it is up to the domain to decide how they want to implement it. Example:

1. they could use an endpoint in BE that expects customerId in either payload or query param \(and hence we can simply reuse it completely, and define it as proxy endpoint in BFF\)
2. they could set context using CustomerProvider, and call the endpoint in BE that expects customerId from context instead \(and if not available, 500 error is rightfully thrown\)

I would prefer \(1\) instead and we stick to setting TenantId/CustomerId/EmployeeId context by auth only.

**Concern stated in the source:** This logic actually exists in `InitiateFeeRedemptionCmdHandler`, it’s best we rely on sequence of events, rather than duplicating it again.

The communication logic in fact can be region agnostic as well \(the same way `InitiateFeeRedemptionCmdHandler` doesn’t care about sg or hk\). We can simply use the `redemptionDetails` \(instead of using amount from `discountDetails`, and having to assume that there is no tax involved\)

```
event.feeChargeRequest.redemptionDetails match {
  case Some(redemptionDetails) =>
    redemptionDetails.redeemedAmount match {
      case Some(chargeAmount) =>
        ...communication logic goes here...
      case None =>
        logger.error("... <unexpected-please-check> ... ")
        Future.successful(Done)
    }
  case None =>
    // waived without vouchers
    Future.successful(Done)
}
```

## A2-0821 — ProductPortfolioRepository: Maybe we can keep this method generic, but only handle for CoreEnhanced for now…

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9605 ([INV-3236] feat(advisory): create advisory endpoints for goal create), advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/entities/portfolio/db/repository/ProductPortfolioRepository.scala; original row 821.

**Concern stated in the source:** Maybe we can keep this method generic, but only handle for CoreEnhanced for now…

```
def findProductPortfolio(
  advisoryTag: AdvisoryTag,
  riskTarget: ModelPortfolioRiskTarget,
  tradingAccountType: TradingAccountType
): Future[ProductPortfolio] = {
  findAllActiveForAdvisoryTag(advisoryTag)
    .filter(p => filterForTradingAccountType(advisoryTag, tradingAccountType, p))
    .filter(p => filterForRiskTarget(advisoryTag, riskTarget, p))
    .runWith(Sink.headOption)
    .flatMap({
      case Some(productPortfolio) => Future.successful(productPortfolio)
      case None =>
        Future
          .failed(BadRequest(s"Unable to find $advisoryTag portfolio for trading account $tradingAccountType with risk target of $riskTarget"))
    })
}

private def filterForRiskTarget(advisoryTag: AdvisoryTag, riskTarget: ModelPortfolioRiskTarget, p: ProductPortfolio): Boolean = {
  advisoryTag match {
    case AdvisoryTag.CORE_ENHANCED =>
      ProductPortfolio.extractCoreEnhancedMetaData(p).exists(_.riskTarget == riskTarget)
    case _ => false
  }
}
```

‌

I want to keep the method signature as close to the lookup by targetStockRatio one so it’s easier to switch later for Flagship/Esg/Factors/FlagshipDpm

## A2-1059 — PageDataGenerator: Actually we have too many region pattern matching in this method. Maybe consolidate it a bit

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9052 ([INV-3010] : update monthly statement to include dpm section), report-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/report/impl/statement/data/statementDataGenerator/goalBasedStatement/PageDataGenerator.scala; original row 1059.

**Concern stated in the source:** Actually we have too many region pattern matching in this method. Maybe consolidate it a bit

```
def headTailMapper(...)

def generate(goals: List[GoalRowDetails], isDPM: Boolean, maxRowsInFirstPage: Int, firstPageTemplate: String, subsequentPageTemplate: String): List[(AllInvestmentGoalsPageData, String)] = ...

region match {
  case SilverRegion.Sg =>
    // SG AllInvestmentGoals templates do not distinguish DPM and non-DPM goals, hence treating all goals as non-DPM
    generate(
      goals = pageData.goalDetails.asScala.toList,
      isDPM = false,
      maxRowsInFirstPage = maxRowsPerAllInvestmentsPage,
      firstPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPage",
      subsequentPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPureGoalsPage"
    )
  case SilverRegion.Hk =>
    // HK AllInvestmentGoals templates have special empty page
    if (pageData.goalDetails.isEmpty) {
      List((pageData.copy(goalDetails = pageData.goalDetails), "allInvestmentGoalsPageWithoutGoal"))
    } else {
      val allInvestmentDPMPageData = generate(
        goals = pageData.goalDetails.asScala.toList.filter(_.isDiscretionary),
        isDPM = true,
        maxRowsInFirstPage = maxRowsPerAllInvestmentsPageForFirstDPMPage,
        firstPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPage",
        subsequentPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPureGoalsPage"
      )
      val allInvestmentNonDPMPageData = generate(
        goals = pageData.goalDetails.asScala.toList.filterNot(_.isDiscretionary),
        isDPM = false,
        maxRowsInFirstPage = maxRowsPerAllInvestmentsPage,
        firstPageTemplate = "allInvestmentNonDPMGoalsPage",
        subsequentPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPureGoalsPage"
      )
      allInvestmentDPMPageData ++ allInvestmentNonDPMPageData
    }
  case _ => throw new Exception(s"AllInvestmentGoalsPageData generator behaviour not configured for region $region.")
}
```

‌

## A2-1083 — Review: Trading team will:

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> PR 9296 ([INV-3070] revert(advisory): revert fx supported ccy validation in advisory endpoint), no inline path; original row 1083.

**Concern stated in the source:** Trading team will:

* add supported ccy validation for indicative quote
* after cash reservation is accepted, this is validated again before we make the actual fx conversion - if error, will block the trade. TradeOps then can intervene as usual, i.e. delete/cancel the trade

‌

The above scenario can happen even if we add this validation in advisory. Example: ccy X is supported on T, we allow goal creation…. T\+1 something is wrong, and we remove support for that ccy… T\+2 investment is funded, and fxconversion will now fail

> * after cash reservation is accepted, this is validated again before we make the actual fx conversion - if error, will block the trade. TradeOps then can intervene as usual, i.e. delete/cancel the trade
> 
> ‌
>

**Conditions and limits:**

- Supported FX currencies may change between goal creation T, removal T+1 and funding T+2; advisory-time validation cannot prevent this. Revalidate before actual conversion, block trade on failure, and TradeOps can cancel/delete.

## A2-1205 — Startup: How about we decouple cluster startup from onMemberUp callback \(potentially can provide 0 or more than 1 callbacks\)

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9049 (DYNAMIC-1046: Terminate service if onMemberUp fails (ready for review)), akka-silver-commons/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/commons/startup/Startup.scala; original row 1205.

**Concern stated in the source:** How about we decouple cluster startup from onMemberUp callback \(potentially can provide 0 or more than 1 callbacks\)

We can follow akka Cluster approach, essentially just wrap it with additional akka management etc. and handle error in callback to terminate system

```
class AkkaClusterStartup(system: ActorSystem[_]) {
  AkkaManagement(system).start()
  AppConfigExtension(system.classicSystem).start()
  ClusterBootstrap(system).start()

  private val cluster = Cluster(system)

  def registerOnMemberUp[T](onMemberUp: => T): Unit = {
    cluster.registerOnMemberUp {
      Try(onMemberUp).recover {
        case e: Exception =>
          logger.error(s"System ${system.name} terminating, akka cluster registered OnMemberUp failed: ${e.getMessage}", e)
          system.terminate()
      }
    }
  }
}

object AkkaClusterStartup {

  def apply(system: ActorSystem[_], onMemberUpCallbacks: (=> Unit)*): AkkaClusterStartup = {
    val clusterStartup = new AkkaClusterStartup(system)
    onMemberUpCallbacks.foreach(cluster.registerOnMemberUp)
    clusterStartup
  }

}
```

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> How about we decouple cluster startup from onMemberUp callback \(potentially can provide 0 or more than 1 callbacks\)
> 
> We can follow akka Cluster approach, essentially just wrap it with additional akka management etc. and handle error in callback to terminate system
> 
> ```
> class AkkaClusterStartup(system: ActorSystem[_]) {
>   AkkaManagement(system).start()
>   AppConfigExtension(system.classicSystem).start()
>   ClusterBootstrap(system).start()
> 
>   private val cluster = Cluster(system)
> 
>   def registerOnMemberUp[T](onMemberUp: => T): Unit = {
>     cluster.registerOnMemberUp {
>       Try(onMemberUp).recover {
>         case e: Exception =>
>           logger.error(s"System ${system.name} terminating, akka cluster registered OnMemberUp failed: ${e.getMessage}", e)
>           system.terminate()
>       }
>     }
>   }
> }
> 
> object AkkaClusterStartup {
> 
>   def apply(system: ActorSystem[_], onMemberUpCallbacks: (=> Unit)*): AkkaClusterStartup = {
>     val clusterStartup = new AkkaClusterStartup(system)
>     onMemberUpCallbacks.foreach(cluster.registerOnMemberUp)
>     clusterStartup
>   }
> 
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌

## A2-1239 — DetectExpiredInvestmentRequestProcessor: [person] [person] [person] Is the below correct understanding?

**Source stance:** open-question

**Concern stated in the source:** [person] [person] [person] Is the below correct understanding?

* autofx: If `fxConversionRequestId` is available here, it means cash is reserved for fx conversion, and we will ensure the conversion will happen. Hence, we will not expire the investment, regardless of `isRequestExpired`. If for whatever reason, the conversion cannot happen,  investment is cancelled elsewhere \(with adequate alerts if needs to manually cancel\).
* autofund: if `autoFundInstruction` is available here, we will ensure the deposit will happen. If there are failures, retry logic will consider expiry \+ cutOff into retry date. Hence, we will not expire the investment, regardless of `isRequestExpired`. And similarly, if for whatever reason, the deposit cannot happen,  investment is cancelled elsewhere \(with adequate alerts if needs to manually cancel\).

## A2-1292 — ValidationHelpers: We can extract amount validation into a method

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 8933 (Feat/INV-2808/flagship dpm goal create endpoints), advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/productline/helpers/ValidationHelpers.scala; original row 1292.

**Concern stated in the source:** We can extract amount validation into a method

```
  def validateAmountRestriction(maybeAmount: Option[BigDecimal], maybeRestriction: Option[SubscriptionAmountRegulation], context: String): Future[Done] = {
    maybeRestriction match {
      case Some(restriction) =>
        val expectedAmount = adjustAmount(maybeAmount, restriction)
        if (maybeAmount != expectedAmount) {
          Future.failed(BadRequest(s"$context breaches amount restrictions: request $maybeAmount, expected $expectedAmount"))
        } else {
          Future.successful(Done)
        }
      case None =>
        Future.successful(Done)
    }
  }
```

‌

And let caller decide how to extract amount \+ restriction, then handle Option themselves.

We can additionally create another method to extract amount for `PlanInvestmentBasedRequest` or `PlanUpsertInvestmentBasedRequest` if needed

## A2-1367 — MarketDataUploader: If we propagate the failure in these places, it will stop the whole flow processing. I suppose we just want to skip?

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 8931 ([INV-2849] create a reconcile job to check instrument prices), marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/utils/MarketDataUploader.scala; original row 1367.

**Concern stated in the source:** If we propagate the failure in these places, it will stop the whole flow processing. I suppose we just want to skip?

If we use `runWithReporting`, we can potentially write sth like this

```
Source(instrument)
  .mapAsync(parallelism) { instrument =>
    reconcilePrices(instrument) // extract this whole pricing fetching + compare into a method
      .map(_ => Right(Done))
      .recover {
        case ex =>
          logger.error("meaningful log message", ex)
          Left(instrument.id)
      }
  }
  .runWithReporting("meaningful context")
```

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> If we propagate the failure in these places, it will stop the whole flow processing. I suppose we just want to skip?
> 
> If we use `runWithReporting`, we can potentially write sth like this
> 
> ```
> Source(instrument)
>   .mapAsync(parallelism) { instrument =>
>     reconcilePrices(instrument) // extract this whole pricing fetching + compare into a method
>       .map(_ => Right(Done))
>       .recover {
>         case ex =>
>           logger.error("meaningful log message", ex)
>           Left(instrument.id)
>       }
>   }
>   .runWithReporting("meaningful context")
> ```
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Per-instrument failures should produce Left(instrument.id) and continue under runWithReporting, rather than fail whole reconciliation.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A3-0094 — Rebalance-in-progress RPC acceptance: modification cancellation versus threshold-breach race

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> rebalance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebalance/impl/entities/rebalancer/handlers/AcceptSuggestedRebalanceRequestCmdHandler.scala; PR: [INV-1504] feat(goal)(rebalance): Avoid race condition for TAA update between goal modification vs RPC acceptance

**Concern stated in the source:** if due to threshold breach, then it’s possible because we don’t block today

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> So if rebalance plan side has its entity updated to rebalance-in-progress \(outer if\):
> 
> 1. if due to goal modification, that cmd handler should have already cancelled the RPC, here it should fail at `RebalanceSuggestionAcceptableStatuses` check
> 2. if due to threshold breach, then it’s possible because we don’t block today

## A3-0218 — Lagom/removed-Lagom error-serdes, shared breaker, whitelist and request-timeout verification matrix

**Source stance:** reported-verification

**Context:**

> None; PR: [INV-1974] feat(all-services): Consolidate svc exception serdes + circuit breaker config

**Concern stated in the source:** Able to return custom error json \(so that other services can deserialize\) instead of the default text response.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> ## Test setup
> 
> instrument svc: Lagom-removed with test endpoint
> 
> * serialize error using ServiceErrorCompat
> * its client services deserialize error using `LagomCompatServiceExceptionSerializer`
> 
> ```
>   def testWater(testType: String): Future[Done] = {
>     testType match {
>       case "LagomBadRequest"  => Future.failed(lagomBadRequest("Invalid request"))
>       case "EndowusNotFound"  => Future.failed(apiNotFound("Entity id not found"))
>       case "SvcException"     => Future.failed(InstrumentSvcException("MorningStar down!", InstrumentSvcErrorType.MORNINGSTAR_API_CALL_FAILURE))
>       case "RuntimeException" => Future { Option.empty.get }
>       case "Slow"             => Future { Thread.sleep(20000) }.map(_ => Done)
>       case _                  => Future.successful(Done)
>     }
>   }
> ```
> 
> ```
> restCall(Method.GET, "/api/internal/instrument/test-water?testType", testWater _)
>     .withCircuitBreaker(CircuitBreaker.identifiedBy("shared-testing")),
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> marketdata svc: Lagom with test endpoint
> 
> * serialize error using `LagomServiceExceptionSerializer`
> * its client services also deserialize error using `LagomServiceExceptionSerializer`
> 
> ```
>   override def testWater(testType: String): ServiceCall[NotUsed, Done] = ServiceCall { _ =>
>     testType match {
>       case "LagomBadRequest"  => Future.failed(BadRequest("Invalid request"))
>       case "EndowusNotFound"  => Future.failed(NotFound("Entity id not found"))
>       case "SvcException"     => Future.failed(MarketDataSvcException("MAS down!", MarketDataSvcErrorType.MAS_MAINTENANCE))
>       case "RuntimeException" => Future { List.empty(1) }
>       case "Slow"             => Future { Thread.sleep(20000) }.map(_ => Done)
>       case _                  => Future.successful(Done)
>     }
>   }
> ```
> 
> ```
> restCall(Method.GET, "/api/internal/marketdata/test-water?testType", testWater _)
>     .withCircuitBreaker(CircuitBreaker.identifiedBy("shared-testing")),
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> goal svc: Lagom-removed with test endpoint calling either instrument / marketdata svc
> 
> * serialize error using ServiceErrorCompat
> 
> ```
>   def testWater(service: String, testType: String, handleSvcErr: Boolean): Future[Done] = {
>     service match {
>       case "marketdata" =>
>         marketDataService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>           case e: MarketDataSvcException =>
>             if (handleSvcErr)
>               throw GoalSvcException("Something wrong with MarketData svc", GoalSvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>             else throw e
>         }
>       case "instrument" =>
>         instrumentService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>           case e: InstrumentSvcException =>
>             if (handleSvcErr)
>               throw GoalSvcException("Something wrong with Instrument svc", GoalSvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>             else throw e
>         }
>       case _ => Future.successful(Done)
>     }
>   }
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> advisory svc: Lagom with test endpoint calling either instrument / marketdata svc
> 
> * serialize error using `LagomServiceExceptionSerializer`
> * also wrap 4xx to Lagom BadRequest to avoid error logging, but this is optional \(also not in scope of this PR\)
> 
> ```
>   override def testWater(service: String, testType: String, handleSvcErr: Boolean): ServiceCall[NotUsed, Done] = {
>     LagomExceptionWrappedServiceCall { _ =>
>       service match {
>         case "marketdata" =>
>           marketDataService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>             case e: MarketDataSvcException =>
>               if (handleSvcErr)
>                 throw AdvisorySvcException("Something wrong with MarketData svc", AdvisorySvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>               else throw e
>           }
>         case "instrument" =>
>           instrumentService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>             case e: InstrumentSvcException =>
>               if (handleSvcErr)
>                 throw AdvisorySvcException("Something wrong with Instrument svc", AdvisorySvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>               else throw e
>           }
>         case _ => Future.successful(Done)
>       }
>     }
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> instrument svc: Lagom-removed with test heavy endpoints
> 
> ```
>   def testHeavy: Future[Done] = {
>     Future { Thread.sleep(15000) }.map(_ => Done)
>   }
>   
>   Api.testHeavy impl { _ => testHeavy },
>   Api.testHeavyWithShortTimeout impl (_ => testHeavy, CustomTimeoutProcess(10.seconds)),
> ```
> 
> ## Test scenarios
> 
> Verified that error serdes works as expected \(as per `LagomServiceExceptionSerializerSpec` / `LagomCompatServiceExceptionSerializerSpec` / `ServiceErrorCompatSpec` \) for all combinations of:
> 
> * calling various testType in test endpoint of instrument/marketdata
> * calling various testType \+ option to handle underlying SvcException in test endpoint of advisory/goal \(forwarding to instrument/marketdata\)
> 
> Verified that if we use same `CircuitBreaker.identifiedBy("shared-testing")` in both instrument and marketdata endpoints, if one triggers circuit breaker, it will affect the other.
> 
> Verified that exception whitelist works as expected. No circuit breaker triggered for BadRequest/NotFound
> 
> Verified that endpoint specific request timeout works as expected. Able to return custom error json \(so that other services can deserialize\) instead of the default text response.

## A3-0515 — Post-Lagom API contract exception versus actor serializer; goal internal exception pattern unresolved

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> rebalance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebalance/impl/entities/rebalancer/handlers/TriggerThresholdBreachedRebalanceCmdHandler.scala; PR: [INV-1303] feat(rebalance): Increase min backoff to 1.5s

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Yeah this is where the voodoo happens.
> 
> 
> 
> Before:
> 
> * SvcException extends Lagom TransportException which the Lagom ExceptionSerializer knows how to serdes them. The `LagomServiceExceptionHelper` is extra logic to help avoiding sentry spamming
> * This same exception is also used to throw inside entity/cmdHandler. These can be serdes thanks to `JsonSerializer[AdvisorySvcException]`
> 
> 
> 
> After Lagom removal:
> 
> * SvcException in \*-api module are now intended as API contract only. They are converted to HTTP error via `EndpointResultCompat#mapToApiError`
> * akka serdes now is configured as
> 
> ```
> akka {
>   actor {
>     serializers {
>       play-json = "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializer"
>     }
>     serialization-bindings {
>       "akka.Done" = akka-misc
>       "akka.actor.Address" = akka-misc
>       "akka.remote.UniqueAddress" = akka-misc
>       "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializable" = play-json
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> * this is why if we want serdes to work… we need to extends `PlayJsonSerializable` \(all the state/cmd/evt do this\)
> * however, it’s debate-able whether we want to add this to our API contract. You can see none of the services do this, except for goal svc
> 
> 
> 
> Goal svc does it in a subtle way:
> 
> * it creates another `GoalSvcException` inside goal-impl and throw this in entity/cmdHandler
> * this is why serdes works for goal svc \(and only goal svc\)
> * and if such internal GoalSvcException is propagate to http, it converts back to the goal-api GoalSvcException
> 
> ```
>   val ServiceErrorMap: Throwable => Throwable = {
>     case logic.GoalSvcException(message, errorType) => GoalSvcException.toApiError(GoalSvcException(message, errorType))
>     case e: GoalSvcException                        => GoalSvcException.toApiError(e)
>     case e                                          => e
>   }
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> So following goal svc should work - but I’m not sure if this is the right way to do it. Let’s think more before we mass apply this pattern

**Conditions and limits:**

- Source wording is preserved in requested_change; interrogatives and proposals are not settled answers.
- The component path and PR title identify source context only; merged/resolved status is not evidence of implementation or correctness.
- The hunk evidence is source context; symbols or conditions found only there must not be attributed to the comment.
- Detailed before/after Lagom-removal serdes distinction retained. Goal internal GoalSvcException mapping is a possible model explicitly NOT approved for mass adoption.

## A3-0724 — Kafka logger override in conf-reference, then Vault/config-map per-service level

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> report-impl/src/main/resources/logback.xml; PR: [EN-1248] chore(report): custom log config

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> If it’s urgent, I guess we can go ahead with this change for now. However, the better way I think is to change the logback.xml in conf-reference instead
> 
> 
> 
> You can make this override-able by:
> 
> ```
> <logger name="org.apache.kafka" level="${org.apache.kafka.log.level:-WARN}"/>
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> Then in the service you want to override, provide the custom log config as
> 
> ```
> <included>
>   <property name="org.apache.kafka.log.level" value="INFO" />
> </included>
> ```
> 
>   
> This custom file will then be set in Vault in old SG setup, or mount via some config-map in the new kustomize setup

## A3-0821 — Independent dividend files: BadRequest nonretry and bounded TCP/unknown retry

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> dividend-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/dividend/impl/subscribers/HongKongEntitlementDividendTopicSubscriber.scala; PR: TT-1732 change dividendTopic to dividendFileTopic

**Concern stated in the source:** Since we can’t reliably reproduce and fix them, we want to limit the number of retries to avoid blocking the whole topic.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> The ServiceLogic in dividend svc alreadymaps the scenarios it cannot handle the file to BadRequest. So we don’t want to waste time retrying for those case \(’s intention\).
> 
> There could potentially still be other exceptions that not caught by ServiceLogic itself, e.g. the case of big file and the tcp connection got cut during file processing. Since we can’t reliably reproduce and fix them, we want to limit the number of retries to avoid blocking the whole topic. Each dividend file should be independent, so we don’t care about their ordering \(unlike events in other normal topic subscribers\).
> 
> I updated the PR to reflect this change :pray:

**Conditions and limits:**

- Source wording is preserved in requested_change; interrogatives and proposals are not settled answers.
- The component path and PR title identify source context only; merged/resolved status is not evidence of implementation or correctness.
- The hunk evidence is source context; symbols or conditions found only there must not be attributed to the comment.
- BadRequest is intentionally non-retry; other file/TCP failures get bounded retries because dividend files are independent and whole-topic blocking is worse.

## A3-1090 — Projection transient retryWARN versus persistent lag threshold1hr and Sentry flooding

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> dividend-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/dividend/impl/entities/brokerAccount/processors/AutoSellDownDividendProcessor.scala; PR: [EN-311] feat(dividend) publish new email request for dividend

**Concern stated in the source:** Retry is successful, and no one would bother about it
* persistent: exception will keep throwing and event processor would be stuck and keep retrying.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Imagine if exception happens:
> 
> * one-off: exception will be thrown normally, and event processor retries by itself. Event processor would log a WARN log I believe. Retry is successful, and no one would bother about it
> * persistent: exception will keep throwing and event processor would be stuck and keep retrying. We should set up monitoring for event processor lag \(with appropriate lag threshold, currently it’s 1hr for all\) to catch it. If we log error here, sentry will be flooded

**Conditions and limits:**

- Source wording is preserved in requested_change; interrogatives and proposals are not settled answers.
- The component path and PR title identify source context only; merged/resolved status is not evidence of implementation or correctness.
- One-off retry/WARN versus persistent-stuck lag monitoring (then1hr threshold); error log would flood Sentry. Preserve as scoped logging/monitoring rationale.

## R-3412 — JSch connected/isConnected flags and closed socket state are distinct checks

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> silver-commons/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/commons/sftp/PooledChannelFactory.scala; PR 3332: SILVER-12449: Report service improments

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> `Channel#connected` is the logical field when we call connect/disconnect on the Channel. `Channel#isConnected` also checks the `Session#isConnected` flag which again is another field driven by connect/disconnect method.
> 
> ‌
> 
> `Channel#closed` is more about the underlying socket connection.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Typically, these two should correspond with each other, i.e. not connected and closed, or connected and not closed. However, since nothing guarantees, we might as well check both. JSch itself checks both to determine if channel is broken or not.

**Evidence:** anon-2.jsonl:3412 · comment 292733024 · PR 3332 · 2022-04-06

Source path: `silver-commons/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/commons/sftp/PooledChannelFactory.scala`

## R-3445 — PDF upload sends email before documentId persistence; SFTP widens the duplicate window

**Source stance:** open-question

**Context:**

> report-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/report/impl/statement/data/StatementDataGenerator.scala; PR 3217: moves to generate metadata separately

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Something to think about. This app server call to create PDF will actually do 2 things:
> 
> * create the PDF
> * call document service to upload the file to GCP → this will trigger eventually trigger communication to send email
> 
> Existing code, right after this, will persist the documentId to report’s cassandra table - which will be used to determine if reprint is required later on.
> 
> If the pod crashes between these 2 steps, report generation is not idempotent, i.e. duplicate documents created / duplicate emails sent to user.
> 
> ‌
> 
> With this change, we somewhat widen the gap with another step to upload to SFTP. Should we consider uploading to SFTP after we persist? If fail to upload, we can retry? Or the generate metadata file part can also attempt uploading if documentId is in csv data, but not found in SFTP? Or we simply log error, which raise sentry and we manually drop the file - should be infrequent enough?
> 
> ‌

## R-3544 — So the reason why I started with this logging change is: * if everything works, we don't log much and it's all fine * if something is wrong, and we still d

**Source stance:** requested-change

**Context:**

> advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/goalcreate/GoalCreateSummaryBehaviour.scala; PR 2820: Move TimedLogger to silver-commons. Logging with marker

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> So the reason why I started with this logging change is:
> 
> * if everything works, we don't log much and it's all fine
> * if something is wrong, and we still don't log much, it's hard to figure out what's wrong from logs. One would need to check the code extensively or already have the whole flow loaded in their brain.
> 
> By default, with INFO level, the `TimedLogger` would only log if the future succeeds or fails, and in how much time.
> 
> If we dial down INFO to DEBUG, whne issue happens, we already lost the log. Increasing the level to log only helps if we know exactly how to reproduce, which might not be the case.

## R-3567 — StrictLogging versus LazyLogging preference is explicitly minor for a singleton event processor

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/entities/instrument/processors/InstrumentMarketDataEventProcessorForMultiCcy.scala; PR 2790: Feat/SILVER-10779 multiccy monthly changes

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> They are almost identical, except `LazyLogging` will mark the Logger with `lazy` and `transient`
> 
> To mean this means only use LazyLogging if you either:
> 
> * logging not offen, and want to save cost of logger initialization in the general code paths that you won’t log \(in this case we logs as soon as `fxConverterToUse` is called\)
> * want to serialize the object \(in this case we won’t serialize this even processor\)
> 
> Having that said, this is very minor. I should have marked as “Nit” :stuck_out_tongue:
> 
> ‌
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- The StrictLogging preference is explicitly minor and conditional on this singleton event processor logging frequently and not being serialized. Source rows: anon-2.jsonl:3565, anon-2.jsonl:3567.

## R-3610 — FX daily-price conversion separates missing prior rate from mapping outcome and uses HALF_EVEN scale 2

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/entities/instrument/processors/InstrumentMarketDataEventProcessorForMultiCcy.scala; PR 2600: removes failing when fx rate is not present for instrument price calculation in another ccy

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Nit: This log doesn’t feel right, cuz now we club the case when fxRateToUse is None, and then case when `.map(fxRateToUse => { blah } `produces None. I know it’s not possible for that map to produce None, but still :stuck_out_tongue: 
> 
> ‌
> 
> Maybe like this is better?
> 
> ```
> convertedDailyPrices = sortedDailyPrices.flatMap { dailyPrice =>
>   fxRates
>     .filterNot(_._1.isAfter(dailyPrice.priceDate))
>     .sortBy(_._1.toEpochDay)
>     .lastOption match {
>       case None =>
>         log.error(s"unable to find the fx rate [$instrumentCcy|$targetCcy] for the date [${dailyPrice.priceDate}], skipping for the date")
>         None
> 
>       case Some(fxRateToUse) =>
>         val convertedPrice = (dailyPrice.value * fxRateToUse._2).setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN)
>         Some(DailyPrice(businessDate = dailyPrice.businessDate, priceDate = dailyPrice.priceDate, priceCcy = targetCcy, value = convertedPrice))
>     }
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
